  "text": "Every Thursday, the museum received a postcard from a city that no longer existed.

Ada filed them beneath Donations Pending Review. It was the closest category she could find.

The postcards showed ordinary things: a tram beside a fountain, laundry above a narrow street, a bakery with green shutters. On the back, in the same careful handwriting, someone always wrote: We are still here.

The city had vanished in 1911. Not burned or flooded. Vanished. Surveyors found wheat fields where its railway station should have been, and the tracks ended neatly at a hedge.

This Thursday’s postcard showed the museum.

Ada recognized the cracked front steps, the stone lions, the window of her basement office. Behind that window stood a woman whose face had been scratched away.

The message was different, too.

Please stop sending people.

Upstairs, a school group clattered through the pottery gallery. Ada could hear their teacher counting them as they passed overhead.

She turned the postcard over again. The museum’s front doors were open. In their shadow, almost too small to distinguish, stood a line of children.

The telephone rang.

“Archives,” she answered.

For a moment she heard only wheels moving over tracks.

Then a child asked, “Is it Thursday there?”

Ada gripped the receiver. Upstairs, the teacher had begun counting again, more slowly.

“Yes,” Ada said.

“Oh, good. Our teacher said someone would be at work.”

“Where are you?”

“Outside the bakery. We can see your lions, but the street keeps getting longer.”

Ada reached for the postcard and looked closely at the children by the doors.

One was holding a telephone."
